evidence.excerpt: The influence of dielectric thickness, copper weight, and layer ordering on radiated emissions from a standardised eight-layer stack-up is evaluated using a parametric FDTD study. A benchmark circuit, consisting of a 500 MHz single-ended clock distribution tree with three fanout nodes, was instantiated on 24 stack-up variants spanning dielectric thicknesses from 0.1 mm to 0.3 mm and copper weights of 0.5 oz and 1 oz. Each variant was simulated to obtain the radiated electric field at 3 m. Stack-ups with the signal layers closest to ground reference planes showed the lowest far-field peak, with a maximum suppression of 8.9 dB relative to the worst-performing arrangement. Dielectric thickness had a stronger influence than copper weight; halving the spacing between a signal layer and its reference plane reduced emissions by an average of 5.2 dB at the fifth harmonic. Simulation time per variant averaged 4.2 hours on a 16-core workstation. The results confirm that stack-up selection is an effective early-stage emission control tool that costs nothing in component budget.
